name: room
description: A data room's own identity. A room is a DTG node, not a row in a host's table: it holds a DID, issues the VIC/VMC/VAC credentials that govern it, and can be messaged. Because a host authorizes room operations against credentials this DID issued — never against its own records — the room is portable: a member simply names a different host, and no credential is reissued. Portability is NOT a matter of re-pointing this document — a room's DID names its mediator, never its host, and deliberately so: a room may be registered with more than one (a mirror serves reads while its primary takes writes), so a host pointer here would not be merely stale but wrong. See rooms/owner/register/0.1 and rooms/keys/backfill/0.1, which both require the caller to name the host. did:webvh rather than did:peer, because a room's controller must be able to change: transferring ownership is a controller change, and did:peer encodes its keys in the identifier so it can never have one. WITNESSES is strongly recommended for any room whose host is not fully trusted — a witnessed log makes a host that serves a stale or suppressed update evident rather than merely possible. MEDIATOR_DID makes the room addressable, which is what lets an invitation, a join, or an epoch notice reach it.
